# Charness v8.16.0

This release ships the task-run lane work that had not been pushed before, led by the new Claude lane executor and its options, together with a fix to the debug planner.

## What changed

- The debug planner reads a `- Risk Class:` value apart from explanatory prose written after it, such as `none yet; ...`, `external-seam (...)` or `none -- ...`. Before this, the whole line was read as the value, so the prose counted as an unknown class. The planner then sent every new investigation in the repository to `repair-risk-declaration` and named another investigation's record as the file to repair. Now a valid value followed by prose is a valid declaration. A new subject starts its own record, and the earlier record stays with its subject. A line that opens with prose, or whose recognized classes include no forced class next to an unknown one, still routes to repair; a forced class next to an unknown one (`external-seam, bogus`) still interrupts, as before. `validate_debug_artifact.py` is unchanged and stays strict.
- `charness task run --executor claude` runs a lane with `claude -p`. Sonnet is the default model, and `--claude-model haiku` selects Haiku. Codex stays the default executor. A Claude lane needs Linux bubblewrap. It runs inside a filesystem sandbox: the lane worktree, its private runtime and explicit `--grant-writable` directories are writable, and home configuration, a named list of credential files (including `~/.docker`, `~/.pypirc` and Cargo credentials; a file outside the list stays readable) and shared Git configuration are not. Container daemon sockets (Docker, containerd, Podman, CRI-O) are masked, so a lane cannot drive the host's container daemon; other host Unix sockets, such as the D-Bus system bus, stay reachable. The sandbox does not restrict network egress: a lane can reach any address the host can, including cloud metadata endpoints ([#889](https://github.com/corca-ai/charness/issues/889)). Provider credentials stay in a parent-side proxy. Commits go to private Git storage that the runner imports into the task branch afterwards, unless the caller grants the checkout's Git common directory, in which case the lane uses the shared linked-worktree Git directly. The result, report, branch, hooks, progress and verification contracts are the same as for other executors. `--grant-writable` now accepts Codex and Claude lanes and still refuses Muse. [docs/claude-task-executor.md](https://github.com/corca-ai/charness/blob/v8.16.0/docs/claude-task-executor.md) states the tested boundary and its limits. The real-sandbox tests ran on Linux with bubblewrap on the release machine; they skip where bubblewrap is absent, and CI does not install it.
- The line that completes a command in a lane's events log now also carries `charness_duration_ms`. For a running lane, `task status <task-id> --commands` also reads the live stdout log, so it shows the current invocation's commands instead of nothing.
- Lane environments: a lane's `TMPDIR`, `TMP` and `TEMP` are now the lane runtime root, so the npm, XDG, pip, ruff, pytest, coverage and pycache paths under it are writable inside a Muse sandbox. Before this, `npm pack` in a Muse lane failed with EROFS. Go's `GOCACHE`, `GOPATH` and `GOMODCACHE` now sit under the lane's cache home, which is private to the lane. A Codex or Claude caller can point it at a shared cache with `CHARNESS_TASK_RUN_CACHE_HOME`, but only inside a directory already granted with `--grant-writable`; the variable never adds a grant. A Codex lane no longer inherits `writable_roots` from the operator's configuration, so only its explicit runtime and `--add-dir` grants are writable, and read-only reviewers drop the lane-only overrides.
- The lane progress rule records the lane's final output after the output capture drains, so the last window's progress counts. A failure of that last observation is ignored only when it is a recoverable I/O error.
- When the Codex app-server exits before answering, the Codex host cache refresh in `charness update` now reports that it exited, instead of a response timeout.
- Windows: runtime snapshots honour the Windows temporary-directory variables, scratch owner locking falls back to Windows byte-range locks where `flock` is missing, reviewer command lines use Windows argument quoting (spaces and quotes; `cmd.exe` metacharacters such as `&` and `%` are not escaped yet, [#890](https://github.com/corca-ai/charness/issues/890)), critique packet producers named `python3` run with the current Python interpreter, and the scratch inventory reports file sizes and repository paths consistently. Linux unit tests cover the argument quoting, interpreter selection and path normalisation; the byte-range lock fallback has no test, CI runs on Linux, and this release claims no run on a Windows host.
- Release repairs to the test suite: these tests, whose verdict depended on machine load, now wait on the event they check. `test_codex_cache_refresh_accepts_real_initialize_shape_and_lifecycle_notifications` (and the other Codex app-server refresh tests) inject the reader's clock and wait for the fake's output instead of a `0.5` s deadline; `test_update_from_explicit_checkout_refreshes_surface` (with the other entry spawn tests) waits for the `charness` process to exit instead of a `28` s bound, and no longer launches a host `codex`; `test_worker_timeout_keeps_started_and_non_approval_state` runs the review wrapper in-process with only the worker's own deadline, so the outer runner bound cannot race it.

## Update

Run `charness update`, then run `charness version` to confirm the installed version. No migration is required. A launcher that relied on a Codex lane writing under a `writable_roots` path from the operator's own Codex configuration must now pass that directory with `--grant-writable`.

def _jsonrpc_child(source: str) -> subprocess.Popen[str]:
    return subprocess.Popen(
        [sys.executable, "-u", "-c", source],
        stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
        text=True,
    )


def _stepped_monotonic(*, step: float) -> tuple[SimpleNamespace, list[float]]:
    """A fake ``time`` module whose ``monotonic()`` starts at 0.0 and advances by
    ``step`` on every call, recording each value it returned. ``step=0.0`` gives a
    clock that never advances (a deadline computed against it can never expire).
    """
    calls: list[float] = []
    state = {"value": 0.0}

    def monotonic() -> float:
        value = state["value"]
        calls.append(value)
        state["value"] += step
        return value

    return SimpleNamespace(monotonic=monotonic), calls

    """The wait is driven by one absolute deadline checked against a clock, not by
    real elapsed time. Replace the loaded module's ``time`` with a fake clock that
    advances a fixed 1000s step on every call, so the number of clock checks the
    deadline math performs before giving up is exact and derivable from the code:
    with deadline=2500 the clock returns 0, 1000, 2000, 3000 -- the first three
    leave `remaining > 0` (one non-matching line consumed each time) and the
    fourth makes `remaining = deadline - monotonic() <= 0`, so the function raises
    on its fourth clock check without touching select/readline again. The step is
    large on purpose: `remaining` is also the real `select` timeout, so a small
    step would let a slow child start turn the third read into a select timeout
    and shorten the sequence -- a wall-clock dependency in disguise. At hundreds
    of seconds the select simply blocks until the child's next line. The child
    emits an unbounded stream of non-matching messages so the outcome cannot
    depend on how many of them it managed to print before being torn down.
    """
    fake_time, calls = _stepped_monotonic(step=1000.0)
    # The wait clock lives in scripts/cli/install_delivery.py
    # (`read_jsonrpc_line_before`): patch the namespace the payload calls,
    # not the loaded entry copy.
    import scripts.cli.install_delivery as install_delivery

    monkeypatch.setattr(install_delivery, "time", fake_time)
    proc = _jsonrpc_child(
        "import json\nwhile True:\n print(json.dumps({'id': 99, 'result': {}}), flush=True)\n"
    )
    try:
        with pytest.raises(_TreeCharnessError, match="timed out"):
            cli_host_codex_rpc.wait_for_jsonrpc_response(
                proc,
                expected_id=2,
                deadline=2500.0,
            )
    finally:
        proc.terminate()
        proc.wait(timeout=2)

    assert calls == [0.0, 1000.0, 2000.0, 3000.0]

def _wait_on_app_server_events(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, *, clock=lambda: 0.0) -> None:
    """Make the response wait a function of the fake's output, never of wall time.

    The reader's deadline and its `select` timeout are its two wall-clock inputs.
    A frozen clock keeps the deadline in the future and `select` blocks until the
    fake actually writes, so a slow interpreter start under load cannot turn a
    response into a timeout. A caller that wants the timeout passes a clock that
    has already passed the deadline.
    """
    import select as real_select

    import scripts.cli.install_delivery as install_delivery

    fake_time = SimpleNamespace(monotonic=clock)
    monkeypatch.setattr(cli_host_codex_rpc, "time", fake_time)
    monkeypatch.setattr(install_delivery, "time", fake_time)
    monkeypatch.setattr(
        install_delivery,
        "select",
        SimpleNamespace(select=lambda read, write, error, _timeout: real_select.select(read, write, error)),
    )

def test_the_shape_packet_validates_the_artifact_this_run_writes(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    """The emitted command must answer the question the packet's own label asks.

    `debug-artifact-shape` calls itself a schema gate for the current artifact and
    emitted the whole-corpus command, so its exit code reported the state of the entire
    historical debug directory instead. A consumer wrote a valid record, saw it reported
    validated, and still got exit 1 from unrelated legacy debt -- with nothing in the exit
    code to say the failure was not theirs.

    Asserted against the scaffold's own write path rather than a literal, so a scaffold
    that routes the write elsewhere (the resolved-followup and subject-refusal arms both
    do) cannot leave the gate pointed at a file nothing writes.
    """
    repo = tmp_path / "repo"
    write_adapter(repo)

    payload = run_plan(repo)

    write_path = payload["scaffold"]["write_artifact_path"]
    shape = next(p for p in payload["gate_packets"] if p["id"] == "debug-artifact-shape")
    assert shape["command"].endswith(f"--paths {write_path}")
    # The scaffold packet's own validator command names the same artifact. Two packets in
    # one plan disagreeing about what is being judged is the state this repairs.
    scaffold_packet = next(p for p in payload["gate_packets"] if p["id"] == "debug-artifact-scaffold")
    assert scaffold_packet["validator_command"].endswith(f"--paths {write_path}")
